# Sluice.go

> A Go library for streaming data in batches: two core types, Stream[T] and
> Batch[T], operators placed by what they retain between two batches, and a
> periphery by external system — a PostgreSQL connector, native HTTP/1.1, 2
> and 3, a QUIC transport, and a web layer that groups handler calls into
> batches. The batch is the unit of transport, never the element. Go 1.26 or
> newer; the standard library plus golang.org/x/crypto and golang.org/x/text.

Start with the index, which sorts every page by what the reader wants to do.

## Docs

- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): every page, by use.
- [Getting started](docs/guide/getting-started.md): install, a first pipeline, the rules a batch follows.
- [Operators](docs/guide/operators.md): what each operator keeps in memory.
- [PostgreSQL](docs/guide/postgres.md): connecting, reading as a stream, writing in batches, replication.
- [Redis and Valkey](docs/guide/redis.md): one connection, a batch of commands in one round trip.
- [NATS JetStream](docs/guide/nats.md): a pull consumer read in batches, acknowledged by your code.
- [Files](docs/guide/files.md): CSV and JSON Lines in batches, each record bounded.
- [Web](docs/guide/web.md): handlers, diagnostics, gateway, authentication, a clean stop.
- [Native HTTP](docs/guide/httpstream.md): net/httpstream over HTTP/1.1, 2 and 3.
- [Deployments](docs/guide/deployments.md): behind a proxy, TLS in front, what to watch.
- [Limits](docs/guide/limits.md): what is not done, and why.
